tutorials.title: Multiworld Setup Guide
tutorials.description: A guide to installing FTL, Hyperspace and the Archipelago mod, and to joining a multiworld.
tutorials.text:
# FTL: Faster Than Light Setup Guide

## Current status

The mod connects to a real Archipelago server and plays a full multiworld on **Linux** and **Windows**.

Hyperspace's Lua sandbox has no sockets and no file access, so the mod cannot talk to a server on its own. You
need this project's **Hyperspace build with the Archipelago module**, not the regular Hyperspace release. It is
the same Hyperspace with one extra module; everything else behaves the same.

## Required software

- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases/latest) 0.6.7 or newer, on the machine
  that generates the seed and hosts the room.
- **FTL: Faster Than Light, Advanced Edition**: 1.6.13 on Linux (what Steam ships), 1.6.9 on Windows, the
  only Windows version Hyperspace runs on. ftlman downgrades the Steam version by itself when it installs
  Hyperspace.
- [ftlman](https://github.com/afishhh/ftlman) to install Hyperspace and apply the mods.
- `Hyperspace.ftl`, from the official [Hyperspace release](https://github.com/FTL-Hyperspace/FTL-Hyperspace/releases)
  1.23.1.
- This project's own build of the Hyperspace library with the Archipelago module: `Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so`
  on Linux, `Hyperspace.dll` on Windows. Then `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` (the mod) and `ftl.apworld`. They are
  attached to the project's GitHub release, or can be built from source with `hyperspace-patch/build.sh`,
  `mod/install.sh` and `apworld/tools/build_apworld.py` (see the project's README for the build dependencies).

## Before you touch anything

**Turn off Steam Cloud for FTL** (right-click the game in Steam, Properties, General). Steam Cloud can overwrite
the save folder while the mod runs.

**Back up your save folder**: `~/.local/share/FasterThanLight/` on Linux,
`Documents\My Games\FasterThanLight` on Windows.

```sh
cp -r ~/.local/share/FasterThanLight ~/.local/share/FasterThanLight.backup
```

The mod plays on a profile of its own (`hs_ap_prof.sav`) and never touches your vanilla `ae_prof.sav`.

**Advanced Edition content must be on.** Ship selection has a toggle for it. The seed hands out the Lanius
cruiser, hacking, mind control, the clone bay and the backup battery, none of which exist with it off. The main
menu reminds you in orange if it is off.

## Installing on Linux

The game lives in `~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/FTL Faster Than Light/`, and everything happens in its
`data` subfolder. From the root of this project:

```sh
D=~/.steam/steam/steamapps/common/"FTL Faster Than Light"/data

# 1. Install the official Hyperspace 1.23.1. This edits data/FTL to preload the Hyperspace library.
ftlman hyperspace-install 1.23.1 -d "$D"

# 2. Build the Hyperspace library with the Archipelago module and drop it in place of the official one
#    (the official .so is kept next to it, as *.before-archipelago).
hyperspace-patch/build-linux.sh --install

# 3. Put Hyperspace.ftl in ~/.local/share/ftl-mods/, then build and apply both mods, Hyperspace first.
mod/install.sh
```

With the release files instead of a source build, steps 2 and 3 become:

```sh
cp "$D/Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so" "$D/Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so.before-archipelago"
cp Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so "$D/"
ftlman patch -d "$D" ~/.local/share/ftl-mods/Hyperspace.ftl ArchipelagoFTL.ftl
```

`mod/install.sh` runs that same `ftlman patch` for you. That command always
rebuilds `ftl.dat` from `ftl.dat.vanilla`, so applying only `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` on its own would remove
Hyperspace from the game.

**Launch the game through Steam or through its `FTL` script**, not `data/FTL.amd64` directly: only the script
preloads Hyperspace. The main menu then shows `HS-1.23.1 x64` in the top right corner, the Archipelago title
and logo at the top left, and a connection panel at the bottom left.

## Installing on Windows

The game lives in `steamapps\common\FTL Faster Than Light` of your Steam library, next to `FTLGame.exe`.
Everything goes in that folder; there is no `data` subfolder on Windows.

1. With ftlman, install Hyperspace 1.23.1 (Hyperspace tab, or `ftlman hyperspace-install 1.23.1 -d <game folder>`).
   On a Steam copy it downgrades FTL to 1.6.9 first and keeps the original as `FTLGame_orig.exe`.
2. Keep a copy of the official `Hyperspace.dll` from the game folder, then put this project's
   `Hyperspace.dll` in its place.
3. Put `Hyperspace.ftl` and `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` in ftlman's `mods` folder, Hyperspace first in the order,
   and apply.

From a source build, in Git Bash, steps 2 and 3 are:

```sh
hyperspace-patch/build-windows.sh --install
FTLMAN=/path/to/ftlman.exe mod/install.sh
```

Both find the game through Steam's library list, `FTL_DATA` / `FTL_DIR` point them elsewhere. The build runs
in Hyperspace's Docker container, so Docker Desktop is needed. FTL has to be closed while installing: Windows
locks `ftl.dat` and `Hyperspace.dll` while the game runs.

The main menu then shows `HS-1.23.1` in the top right corner and the same Archipelago title, logo and panel.

## Installing the apworld

Drop `ftl.apworld` into the `custom_worlds` folder of your Archipelago installation. Only the machine that
generates the seed needs it.

## Generating a seed

Create your YAML with **ArchipelagoOptionsCreator** (in the Archipelago Launcher) or start from a file in
`presets.zip`, put it in `Players/`, and generate as for any
other game. The options worth a second look:

- **Sectorsanity**, **Sectorsanity First Sector** and **Sectorsanity Last Sector** decide how big the seed is.
- **Archipelago Shop Checks** puts goods for other players on sale at one AP STORE beacon per sector. Each
  slot is one check, and the cheapest kind: scrap, no fight. The number is a minimum: when your options create
  more items than checks, the seed adds shop slots until every item has a place. With **Archipelago Shop by
  Sector** (off by default) each slot belongs to one sector and is sold there only.
- **Minimum Filler** is the other side of that balance: filler added when there are more checks than items.
- **Shop Weapons / Shop Drones / Shop Augments** decide how much of FTL's catalogue Archipelago controls, all of
  it by default. **Shop Unlock Mode** decides what that means: `rarity_boost` (default) makes a received item
  more common in stores, `locked` keeps an item off every shelf until you receive it.
- **Systemsanity** turns installing systems into checks (`first_install`), or every level too (`every_level`).
- **Crew Checks** makes the first recruit of each race a check (the starting crew does not count).
- **Crew Members** puts crew members in the item pool; weapons and drones come twice, the second copy adding
  them to the menu that opens at the start of every run.
- **System Blueprints** and **Progressive System Upgrades** decide whether you need a blueprint to buy a system,
  and whether its levels come from Archipelago. With both off, systems behave as in the base game.
- **Goal**, **Victories Required** and **Victory Difficulty** say when you are done. The difficulty is enforced:
  an easy win still sends its victory check, it just does not count towards the goal.
- **Archives** and **Archives Required** add a second currency: Archives scattered through the other players'
  worlds, of which the Flagship waits for a number. Leave a few spare.
- **Death Link**, **Energy Link** and **Trap Link** connect your runs to the other players.

## Connecting to a room

On the main menu, the panel at the bottom left takes the server address, the port, your slot name and the room
password. Press ENTER or click the button. `TAB` moves between fields.

- A successful connection is remembered: next time the fields are filled in. The password never is.
- Tick **auto-connect** to reconnect on every launch.
- If the connection drops, the mod retries on its own (after 5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 seconds).
- Once connected the panel folds into a **Disconnect** button, which brings the panel back.

**Changing seed.** Hyperspace can unlock a ship but never lock one again, so a profile that played another seed
keeps its ships. When you connect to a different seed with such a profile, the mod refuses the seed and asks.
"Yes" makes a dated copy of your profile next to it, erases the Archipelago progress and restarts FTL on its
own (through Steam if you launched it from Steam, on Linux and Windows alike); the new seed begins from nothing. "No" keeps everything and plays the new seed with the old ships.
The same question comes up the first time you connect with a profile that already unlocked ships without
Archipelago.

## Playing

Pick a ship in the hangar (locked ships are simply not there) and play. The mod does the rest:

- Reaching a sector, earning an achievement, installing a system and destroying the Flagship send their checks.
- Ships and layouts you receive appear in the hangar when you return to the main menu, never mid-run.
- Head starts apply at the beginning of each run.
- A system you have no blueprint for cannot be bought: if a store sells you one anyway, the mod removes it and
  refunds exactly the scrap you paid.
- The beacon marked **AP STORE** on the map holds the Archipelago shop; beacons marked **ARCHIPELAGO** hold one of
  five encounters. The Slug in one of them sells a real Archipelago hint.
- Hints about your world, whoever asked for them, show up in game and in the dashboard.

`TAB` opens the dashboard during a run and pauses the game. Its pages: an overview (goal, checks, links,
latest items), the ship layouts, the systems, the checks still to do by category, and a journal of the items
received and the hints. Left/Right or 1-5 change page, the wheel scrolls the lists, Esc closes it.

Losing a run costs you only the run. Your items are kept.

## Playing offline: solo mode

Without a server, click **Solo mode** in the connection panel. Solo mode applies the slot data of a real generated seed and hands
out its items one per check, in the order a real fill produced. It is a way to try the loop and the pacing
alone. It is always the same demo seed shipped with the mod, not your YAML: your options do not apply. A check
that held another player's item in that seed gives filler instead, so every check gives something.

A solo run is saved in the FTL profile: the items received and the checks sent survive a restart, and a solo
run that was going when FTL closed picks up again at the next launch. **Stop solo** puts it aside; clicking
**Solo mode** later asks whether to continue it or start over.

## Troubleshooting

**The game hangs on the loading screen at 100% CPU.** A Hyperspace bug with an `ae_prof.sav` that was created but
never played. Delete `ae_prof.sav` and any `hs_*_prof.sav` from the save folder and launch again.

**The connection panel is missing, or nothing connects.** The Hyperspace library is the official one, not the
build with the Archipelago module, or Hyperspace is not loaded at all. Check `data/FTL_HS.log`: it should contain
`[AP-net] network module present`.

**My unlocks disappear between sessions.** Steam Cloud is still enabled, or the mods were re-applied without
Hyperspace.

**"Failed to make copy of original code executable" at launch on Linux.** SELinux (Fedora and others) refuses
Hyperspace the right to patch the game in memory. Run `sudo setsebool -P selinuxuser_execheap 1` (and, if the error
stays, `sudo setsebool -P selinuxuser_execmem 1`), then start again. No need to turn SELinux off.

**Where is the log?** `FTL_HS.log` in the game folder (in `data/` on Linux), rewritten at every launch. Lines
from the mod start with `[AP`.

readme.text:
FTL Archipelago

FTL: Faster Than Light in an Archipelago multiworld.
Your ships, systems and weapons are hidden in your friends' games. Theirs are hidden in yours.

For the base game and for FTL: Multiverse beta

English · Français · Deutsch · Español · Italiano · Português

Download · Download for Multiverse
Setup: Windows · Linux
Guides: Playing · Options · FAQ · Discord

Need help? Ask on the Discord, or open an issue with your FTL_HS.log.

> I'm French. This page was written in French, then translated into English with AI. | FTL: Faster Than Light | FTL: Multiverse beta | |---|---| | ![Main menu](docs/images/main-menu.jpg) | ![Multiverse main menu](docs/images/mv-main-menu.jpg) | | 10 ships, 28 layouts, the full base game | all 55 Multiverse ships, the Magic Hat, endings and quests as checks. [More](#ftl-multiverse-beta) | ## How it plays You start with one ship and almost nothing. The other ships, the systems, weapons, drones, augments and crew are scattered across the multiworld. Every run you play sends checks to your friends: reaching a sector, winning a fight, recruiting a race, an achievement, the Flagship. What they find for you arrives on its own, and losing a run only costs the run. | | | |---|---| | ![Locked ships in the hangar](docs/images/hangar.jpg) | ![The start-of-run menu](docs/images/start-menu.jpg) | | ![The Archipelago shop](docs/images/shop.jpg) | ![AP STORE and Archipelago beacons on the map](docs/images/map.jpg) | ## New in 0.6 - **Every seed has its own save**, and a Saves button to switch between them. - **Fights, events and your reactor** can send checks. - **Four new traps** (a hazard, an anti-ship battery, a Flagship power surge, O2 drain) and **two new events**. - **Sector Skip, Sector Locks, Flagship Sabotage** and more options to change how a run feels. - **The dashboard knows the logic**: a blue line marks what you can already do. - A **solo preset**, and **Multiverse** is now its own game. All the details in the [release notes](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/releases/tag/v0.6.0). ## Everything in one key: the dashboard Press **TAB**, in a run or in the hangar. The game pauses and your whole game in the multiworld is there at a glance: - **Your goal** and where you stand. - **Every check, ship by ship and sector by sector.** A blue line marks the ones you can already do with what you have, so you always know where to go next. - **Every item you received**, who sent it, and what was inside each bundle. - **Your hints**: what the others found for you, and where your items wait in their worlds. - **Achievements** with their game icons, **victories** with each ship's picture, the **crew races** you recruited. - **Your links**: Death Link, Trap Link, and the fuel in the shared Energy Link reserve. | | | |---|---| | ![Dashboard overview](docs/images/dashboard-links.jpg) | ![Checks ship by ship](docs/images/dashboard-checks.png) | | ![Ships you own](docs/images/dashboard-ships.png) | ![Achievements on the checks page](docs/images/dashboard-achievements.jpg) | ## What you will run into Every sector has an **AP STORE** that sells packages for the other players, plus deals and blood pacts: scrap now, a trap or a dead crew member later. Other beacons hold Archipelago events: pirates holding a package, a Slug selling real hints, an Engi who bets he can overclock your reactor, a rare arms dealer. ![Blood pacts in the Archipelago shop](docs/images/blood-pacts.jpg) | | | |---|---| | ![The Engi overclock bet](docs/images/event-overclock.jpg) | ![The arms dealer](docs/images/event-arms-dealer.jpg) | With **Sector Skip**, a sector you already know starts on an exit beacon: jump right away for scrap and one more pick at the start of the run. ![Sector Skip: the first beacon is an exit](docs/images/sector-skip.jpg) ## In numbers | | | |---|---| | Ships | 10, with 28 layouts | | Checks | about 75 for a first game, 150 by default, several hundred with everything on | | Options | more than 70, and 5 presets from 3 hours to 20 or more | | In game | 11 traps, 7 Archipelago events, an AP STORE in every sector | | Languages | 6 | | With Multiverse | 55 ships, 18 crew races, a Magic Hat with 65 destinations | Want chaos? Put this in your YAML and play with friends: ```yaml trap_chance: 30 trap_link: true death_link: true ``` More ideas and every option on the [options page](docs/wiki/Options.md). ## Getting started 1. Get `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` and the Hyperspace library from the [release](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/releases) and follow the setup page for [Windows](docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.md) or [Linux](docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.md). 2. Make your YAML, or take a [preset](presets). The host needs `ftl.apworld` and Archipelago 0.6.7. 3. Start FTL, fill in the panel at the bottom left and connect. No server? Try **Solo mode**. ## FTL: Multiverse beta Archipelago also runs on top of **FTL: Multiverse 5.5** as its own game, **FTL Multiverse** (`ftl_mv.apworld` and `FTLArchipelago-MV.ftl`, on the releases named `-mv`). Everything from the base mod is there, plus all the Multiverse ships, the Magic Hat to reroute to the sector you choose, Multiverse endings and ship quests as checks, and the AP STORE in the secret sectors too. A ship that starts without Oxygen gets it offered for free. | | | |---|---| | ![AP STORE and Archipelago beacons on a Multiverse map](docs/images/mv-sector-map.jpg) | ![Magic Hat destinations](docs/images/mv-magic-hat-secret.jpg) | | ![The eighteen Multiverse races on the dashboard](docs/images/dashboard-first-crew-mv.png) | ![Multiverse ships on the dashboard](docs/images/mv-ships.jpg) | Install Hyperspace, the two Multiverse zips (Assets, then Data), then `FTLArchipelago-MV.ftl` last in ftlman, and put `ftl_mv.apworld` in `custom_worlds`. More in the [Multiverse page](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/mv-next/docs/wiki/Multiverse.md). ## AI usage FTL Archipelago was made with the help of AI for: - **the Hyperspace library** (`Hyperspace.dll` and the `.so` files), which adds the network layer so FTL can talk to the Archipelago server - **part of the tests**, automatic ones and runs played on Linux and Windows before each beta - **the translations**: everything is written in French first, then translated with AI. The English is checked by the community, the German by Yunus and the Spanish by Trapper444. Italian and Portuguese are still AI only, fixes are welcome. I take full responsibility for the project and its code: I understand how it works, including the parts where AI helped, and I maintain, debug and support it myself. ## Thanks **Where it started.** Before this mod existed, **File_Missing** and **eto** were already bringing FTL to Archipelago with [FTL Multiverse Archipelago](https://github.com/Filemissing/FTLMultiverseArchipelago). File_Missing started that project and the FTL Archipelago Discord, and eto did the research on the Hyperspace API. eto's [FTL Manual](https://github.com/Et0san/Manual) was the starting point of this mod's items and locations. They welcomed this mod with open arms when it showed up. Thank you both. **Translations and art.** **Trapper444** for the Spanish, the logo and the Multiverse Magic Hat, based on his ArchiHat. **Yunus** for the German. **Testing.** **Tom Regor**, for all his testing and logs, the multiworld syncs he runs, and ideas like the O2 Drain Trap and the in logic marker. **Trapper444** and **Rhythm**, for the Multiverse tests and the reports on logic and balance. **ottomaatti**, for getting about ten people to play the mod at a LAN party and sending me a detailed report. **First testers.** **Cigogne** and **SynthKat67**, who took the first bumps in the very early days (empty shops, renaming a crew member that set off Death Link), and **Astron**, there from the start with lots of tests and feedback. **Bug reports.** **threeandthree** (TLS on Steam Linux), **Mulac** (locked shop), **Richard99** (journal), **Nowi** (Death Link), **Mrs. Maple** (GOG on Linux), **Jam** (enemy weapons too strong), **Wyndrose**, **fletchy** and **Mongolico** (crashes and logs). **On the Archipelago Discord.** **roobyroo**, for the warm welcome and the help with the rules. **Ideas and help.** **studkid**, for the design talks (logic, shop names, saves) and for helping players set up. **TheLegendaryDuck** for the anti-ship battery trap idea, which became a real trap of the mod, and **Kholdstare** for the ideas of unlocks by sector. And everyone on the Discord who plays, joins the test syncs, reports bugs and votes on ideas: this mod would not be what it is without you. ## Credits The first design of the items and locations comes from the [FTL Manual by Et0san](https://github.com/Et0san/Manual) (MIT). Built on [FTL: Hyperspace](https://github.com/FTL-Hyperspace/FTL-Hyperspace) (CC-BY-SA 4.0). See `apworld/ftl/LICENSE.md` and `mod/ArchipelagoFTL/CREDITS.md`. Building from source and running the tests: [docs/BUILDING.md](docs/BUILDING.md).

notes.text:
Every seed gets its own save, fights and events send checks, four new traps, two new events, new options to change how a run feels, and a dashboard that knows the logic. Plus a lot of fixes from your reports during the betas.

## Updating from 0.5

1. In ftlman, replace `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` with the one from this page and click Apply.
2. **Copy the Hyperspace library from this page into the FTL folder again**, after Apply: `Hyperspace.dll` (Windows), `Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so` (Linux, Steam) or `Hyperspace.1.6.12.amd64.so` (Linux, GOG/Humble). 0.6 needs this new one.
3. Replace `ftl.apworld` too, and make a new seed: the new options only exist in a seed made with 0.6. Archipelago 0.6.7 is needed.

On Epic, FTL has to be downgraded to 1.6.9 by hand first, see the setup page.

## Saves

- **Every seed has its own FTL save**, one per slot. When you join a new seed the mod asks first, and the old save stays exactly as it was. Your normal FTL save is never touched.
- A **Saves** button on the main menu lists them all, with their checks and when you last played. Load one, run in progress included, or archive it.

## New checks

- **Fights per sector** (`combat_checks_mode: per_sector`): the first fights you win in each sector send their own checks, 1 to 5 per sector.
- **Archipelago Event checks** (`event_checks`, 5 by default): the relay and pirate events hand out their own checks. Every sector gets one of them for sure.
- **Reactor checks** (`reactor_checks`): reactor power 10, 15, 20 and 25.
- Accepting a surrender counts as a fight won, an enemy that jumps away does not.

## New options

- **Sector Skip**: a layout that already reached the next sector can skip sectors 1 to 4. Their first beacon is an exit, and jumping right away gives 60 scrap and one more pick in the start-of-run menu.
- **Sector Locks**: each layout needs two Sector Passes, to leave sector 4 and sector 7.
- **Flagship Sabotage** (0 to 5): each Flagship phase arrives weakened, less hull, shields or weapons.
- **Archipelago Shop Deal Scrap** (0 to 200%): what the deals pay, 0 turns them off.
- **Kestrel Needs Its Key**: when you don't start with the Kestrel, it needs its key like any other ship. Until it comes, the hangar marks it NO KEY and START refuses it.
- **Progressive Unlocks the System**: the first upgrade of a system also unlocks it, so systems come sooner.
- **Layout Unlocks**: `independent` (a Type B or C can come without the A) and `progressive` (one key per layout, A then B then C).
- **Early Ship Keys** (1 by default): a second ship comes early, in your own first checks.
- **Event Beacons**: which beacons say ARCHIPELAGO on the map.
- **Crew Names**: crew who join take the other players' names, or the team's, or FTL's.
- **Archipelago Shop Hints**: what you see at an AP STORE becomes a hint for its owner (on by default).
- **Sector Logic** `relaxed` is now called `none` (old YAMLs still work).
- A new **`solo_game` preset**: about 7 hours, made for one player alone.
- Options are sorted in groups in the Options Creator.

## Traps

- **Hazard Trap**: your next fight's beacon gets a nebula, ion storm, asteroids, a sun or a pulsar.
- **Anti-Ship Battery Trap**: your next fight has a battery shooting at you.
- **Power Surge Trap**: your next enemy gets a Flagship power surge, again every 25 seconds (lighter in sectors 1 and 2).
- **O2 Drain Trap**: every room loses its air at once, never enough to kill a badly hurt crew member.
- Hull Breach Trap makes one real breach in a random room.
- With Trap Link on, a deal's trap goes to another FTL player only when someone is really on the link. Alone it always hits you.

## Events

- **Engi overclock**: an Engi tech bets he can push your reactor further (Engi and civilian sectors).
- **Arms dealer**: rare, in pirate sectors.
- The pirates' package gives a vague word on what it is worth.
- The Zoltan checkpoint costs 15 scrap for 3 fuel.

## Dashboard and menus

- **In logic marker**: a blue line on the checks you can already do with what you received.
- The hangar refuses START on a ship that would not count (out of the seed or not received yet) and says why, and RANDOM SHIP only draws among the ships you have.
- The dashboard opens in the hangar too, on the ships page, sorted by checks left with an "Unlocked only" filter.
- The start-of-run menu shows each weapon and drone's power and stats, lets you pick which systems come aboard when they don't all fit, offers Oxygen for free to a ship that has none, and a Medbay or Clone Bay swap.
- Energy Link shows the shared reserve in fuel and tells you when others put fuel in.
- A crew member received with a full crew waits for a free seat.
- The connect panel has a real cursor: arrows, Home, End, Delete, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+V at the cursor.
- **Universal Tracker** works, without your YAML.

## Fixes

- Locked items and systems really stay out of stores, even with a store opened by an event or Multiverse's store button.
- Death Link: holograms, temporary crew and crew taken away by an event are not deaths, and Death Link can be switched off in game.
- Fights won offline before a crash are sent on the next connection.
- A continued run sends the fights it had counted.
- Run start scrap is given once, even when the run started before connecting.
- Shop packages count spheres from 1, like Archipelago.
- Systemsanity no longer has Install checks for Engines, Oxygen, Piloting and Weapon Control, every ship starts with them.
- Random YAMLs always generate.
- Ships are named by their class in every menu (Federation Cruiser B).

Thanks to Trapper444 and Yunus for the Spanish and German reviews, and to everyone who tested the betas and reported bugs on the Discord.

## How to install

| | |
|---|---|
| **Windows** | [English](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.md) · [Français](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.fr.md) · [Deutsch](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.de.md) · [Español](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.es.md) · [Italiano](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.it.md) · [Português](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Windows.pt.md) |
| **Linux** | [English](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.md) · [Français](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.fr.md) · [Deutsch](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.de.md) · [Español](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.es.md) · [Italiano](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.it.md) · [Português](https://github.com/TheLiloji/FTLArchipelago/blob/main/docs/wiki/Setup-Linux.pt.md) |
